clue.text: Gigantic male donkey carries four to Spain

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
IV is four in Roman numerals
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A huge male donkey is hauling a load of four to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries' and 'to' just string the pieces together in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive and gigantic are synonyms, both meaning of enormous size.

clue.text: Mean, for example, to go back after a very long time

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed after the others

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long period of history

indicators.note: to go back is to run in the opposite direction, so these letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to return after a very long absence, set beside the word 'mean'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb or an adjective for stingy, but it is the statistical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic average of a set of values.

clue.text: Inch removed from some clothes I'd left

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of a part of the following words, a run sitting inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of clothes, the whole of I'd and the start of left

explanation.surface: Someone takes an inch off some clothes they had left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a measurement being trimmed from a garment, but it is a verb: to move slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along furtively, much as to inch forward is to creep a little at a time.

clue.text: Shudder as rival eats black rodent

indicators.note: the first word swallows the others, so they go inside it

parts.note: to vie is to compete, to rival someone
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone shudders as a competitor devours a black rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rival' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning compete.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to shake or quiver rapidly, as a body does when it shudders.

clue.text: Reassure about poor form in bed

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: a poor version is a badly made one, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the four letters of form are taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries to reassure a patient who is in poor shape in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is only a link here, joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to console or soothe them, which is what reassurance does.

clue.text: Toy did turn out to be a queer thing

indicators.note: to turn out a drawer is to empty and rearrange it, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A toy someone made proved to be a strange object.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a strange or peculiar thing, queer in its older sense of odd.

clue.text: New RAF intern giving up home to penniless friend of brother

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so the letters are rearranged
the intern gives up one part in favour of another, swapping it for what follows 'to'

parts.note: the letters of these words, taken as written
IN means at home

indicators.note: without a penny, so the P for penny is dropped

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A new RAF trainee leaves home to live with a broke mate of their brother.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a penny. 'Friend of brother' reads as one person, but 'friend' belongs to the wordplay and 'of brother' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal is the adjective from Latin frater, meaning relating to or like a brother.

clue.text: Article about concert

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, moved around into a fresh order

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written about a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it tells you to rearrange the letters of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, typically by a soloist or small group, so a kind of concert.

clue.text: Selfless penitence is about work for change

indicators.note: the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
less the self, and I is how one refers to oneself, so that letter goes

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written
a piece is a work of art or music

explanation.surface: Penance without ego is about doing work for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' tempts as a phrase, but 'change' alone is the definition: loose coins. The British tenpence piece is a common coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Change means coins, and a tenpence piece is a British coin worth ten pence.

clue.text: It requires many to finish repair

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, which is many
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A repair job that needs a lot of people to complete it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to fix it, the everyday synonym of repair.

clue.text: Sending Queen up in naughty impudence as part of Christmas dinner!

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the next word

parts.note: bad as in badly behaved

indicators.note: with 'up', sending something up in a down clue reads it backwards; here it is used for an across answer too
completes the instruction to reverse the Queen's letters

parts.note: sauce is cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A naughty, cheeky family member mocks the monarch over Christmas dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen. Bread sauce is a British milk-and-breadcrumb sauce served with roast turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread sauce is a traditional British accompaniment to the roast at Christmas dinner, so a component of the meal.

clue.text: Artist arrived before photographer

indicators.note: the word for arrived is placed before the artist

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, to arrive
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The artist got there before the photographer did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Photographer' is a loose definition: the camera is the device that takes the photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the instrument that takes photographs, so it is figuratively the photographer.

clue.text: They may be treated with a theatre trip

definitions.text: They may be treated with a theatre trip

parts.note: on the surface, given a treat, a night out paid for; in fact given medical treatment
seemingly an outing to see a play; really a visit to the operating theatre

explanation.surface: People who might be taken out for an evening at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a treat of a show, but the theatre is a hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients are people who receive medical treatment, sometimes by surgery in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Spring set off binge of contentment

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: set off like a firework, the letters are blown apart and land in a new order

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The arrival of spring sets off a binge of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellbeing is a state of being comfortable, healthy and happy, close to contentment.

clue.text: Washed clothes for the French subeditor

definitions.note: a verb phrase, to have washed clothes, matching the past tense of the answer

parts.note: la is French for 'the'
split as sub, giving UNDER (as in submarine), and editor, giving ED

explanation.surface: Someone washed the clothes for a French subeditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subeditor' must be split in two: sub means under and ED is an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash and iron clothes, so laundered means having washed them.

clue.text: Relative removing cooked crab from the boil

indicators.note: the following letters are taken away from the boil

parts.note: a carbuncle is a severe boil on the skin
cooked as in doctored: the letters of crab rearranged into the run found at the start of the boil

explanation.surface: A family member takes a cooked crab out of the boiling pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boil' looks like boiling water for the crab, but it is a skin abscess.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, a parent's brother, so a relative.

clue.text: Island uses sea for supply

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An island relies on the sea to bring in its supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea' is a terse anagram signal, short for at sea, meaning muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to give out or distribute, as when supplies are issued to troops.

clue.text: Quiet because carrying semi-toxic metal

indicators.note: the first word carries the next piece within it

parts.note: since can mean because
lead is the toxic metal, and semi- takes half of it, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Things are quiet because someone is carrying a mildly poisonous metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Since' as 'because' is the causal sense, not the time one.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is the absence of sound, so quiet, as a noun.

clue.text: Freshen large milky coffee lacking temperature

parts.note: venti is the largest standard cup size at Starbucks

indicators.note: the coffee is without the following letter

parts.note: a latte is coffee made with steamed milk

explanation.surface: Someone tries to perk up with a large latte that has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Venti is the Starbucks name for its large size, from the Italian for twenty (ounces).
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate a room is to let fresh air in, freshening it.

clue.text: Need a drink? Try this cocktail

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender offers a cocktail to someone who wants a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question rather than a word: someone who needs a drink is thirsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thirsty is the feeling of needing something to drink.

clue.text: Philosopher is an aspiring pedlar

parts.note: a tinker was a travelling mender of pots who also sold wares
to aspirate a word is to breathe an aitch into it, so this supplies that breathy letter, placed inside the pedlar

explanation.surface: A philosopher who is really an ambitious door-to-door salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiring' looks like 'ambitious', but it means adding the breathy letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker is someone devoted to ideas, a philosopher in the broad sense.

clue.text: Turf at back half of garden is soaking wet

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf

indicators.note: only the rear half of the word is kept, its front half discarded

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The lawn at the back of the garden is waterlogged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means saturated with water, thoroughly soaked.

clue.text: Laid off in backlog, I get flowers

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: read as back log: the word log written backwards

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laid off with work piled up gets sent flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backlog' must be split as back + log: log reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall plants with sword-shaped leaves and spikes of bright blooms.

clue.text: Damage results from intramuscular brace

parts.note: IM is the medical abbreviation for intramuscular, as in an injection
a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: An injection into a muscle leaves a brace that does harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or harm something, so to damage it.

clue.text: Experimental look into abyss

indicators.note: the word for look goes into the pit

parts.note: a pit is a deep hole, an abyss
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: An experimental peek down into a deep chasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme is a small trial run, so pilot as an adjective means experimental.

clue.text: Unties cord around presents

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a different order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone untying the string wrapped round gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' looks like a noun for gifts, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone is to introduce them formally.

clue.text: Admire Kylie taking year out to travel

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so they are rearranged
with 'out', taking a letter out of the singer's name
completes taking out: the letter is removed

parts.note: the singer's name, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan admires Kylie for taking a gap year to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: Kylie Minogue's first name is just fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: To like someone is to be fond of or think well of them, close to admiring them.

clue.text: Women dined out before grand marriage ceremony

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the final letter
out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word's letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Women went out to dinner before a grand wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: G is a grand, slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is the ceremony at which two people are married.

clue.text: Mr E. is said to be an enigma

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the title and initial give the sound of the word

parts.note: read aloud, Mister E

explanation.surface: A man known only as Mr E. is a riddle to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr E. reads aloud as 'Mister E', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is something puzzling or unexplained, just as an enigma is.
